caption: The drawing depicts an arched structure resembling a decorative doorway or portal. The structure is composed of two vertical columns colored in a reddish-brown hue, each resting on a wide, flattened base, and topped with a capital. The columns support a large sweeping arch that curves upward into two spirals at the ends. The arch and the outline of the columns are also rendered in reddish-brown. The arch is adorned with a border of blue oval shapes on its outer rim. Three crosses, also in reddish-brown, are positioned at the top center and the two top ends of the arch. Along the inner edge of the arch and downward along the columns, there are smaller circles colored in a light beige or off-white shade. The background is plain, with a faint, diffuse grayish shading behind the structure. The artist's signature “George C. Rhone” is located in the lower right corner of the drawing.
title: Wall Painting
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
